title: Launch
slide_intent: Show how a recurring campaign can stay legible over time. A fixed weekly format lets people notice what has changed, while phases help the team decide what to publish next.
strategic_value: Halfkey can tie its launch story to a visible record of keys and receipts. A recurring figure can connect the waitlist, launch announcement and subsequent product activity.
demonstration: A strip of sixteen weekly posters spans weeks 2–17. It sits above a four-phase plan with proposed targets and a $220k budget distributed across five channels.
practical_value: A campaign designer can identify the week’s poster, the phase it serves and the resources allocated to that phase’s distribution channels.

content_islands.name: Running header and campaign idea
content_islands.spec: Place “This week’s key” beneath Campaign idea. Align the weekly publishing premise to its right. Explain that a waitlist dot represents 1,000 people while receipt dots represent money.

content_islands.name: Weekly poster strip
content_islands.spec: Align one equal-width portrait per week from week 2 through week 17. Place week and date beneath each. Group by Tease, Beta, Launch and Sustain, and highlight week 10 in Signal blue.

content_islands.name: Phase plan
content_islands.spec: Place a matrix below the strip with one column per phase and rows for activity and targets. Identify weekly active keys as the north star. Treat the quantities as campaign targets.

content_islands.name: Budget
content_islands.spec: List creators, paid social, OOH, community and events, and PR and content beneath the plan. Align amounts, shares, dot bars and channel notes. State the January–April 2027 total of $220k and the value of $1,000 per dot.
